title: Ketone & DKA model — FFA-driven, two-gate ketogenesis (Cahill / Kitabchi)

caption.scope: FFA-driven ketogenesis and DKA acidosis model implemented in the T1D simulator, structured after the ketone physiology described in Cahill Jr GF, N Engl J Med 282:668-675 (1970) for the two-gate ketogenesis pathway, and DKA severity criteria from Kitabchi et al., Diabetes Care 32:1335-1343 (2009). Plasma insulin I suppresses ketone production at two sequential gates: (1) the lipolysis gate — insulin inhibits hormone-sensitive lipase (HSL) via a Hill function (EC50 = 8 mU/L, n = 3), reducing FFA release from adipose; (2) the CPT-1 gate — insulin raises malonyl-CoA via acetyl-CoA carboxylase (ACC), blocking carnitine palmitoyltransferase-1 and preventing mitochondrial FFA import (EC50 = 8 mU/L, n = 4). Both gates must be open for ketone production: BHB production rate = LIPOLYSIS_MAX * lipolysisGate * ffaLipolysis * cpt1Activity * k_BHB. BHB is removed by Michaelis-Menten oxidation in muscle and brain (exercise-boosted) and by renal excretion above 0.5 mmol/L. Acidosis load accumulates above BHB 3.0 mmol/L with a smoothstep insulin gate that prevents nutritional ketosis from triggering DKA; game over fires when acidosisLoad reaches 600.

variables.definition: plasma insulin concentration (mU/L) — master suppressor of both ketogenic gates
FFA pool released from adipose lipolysis (mmol/L equivalent); separate from dietary ffaBlood; t1/2 approx 60 min via oxidation and re-esterification
plasma beta-hydroxybutyrate (mmol/L); clamped to 0-20 range; dominant circulating ketone body
Michaelis-Menten oxidation sink representing muscle and brain BHB uptake; Vmax = 0.02, Km = 2.0; multiplied by (1 + max(0, deltaHR/120)) during exercise
renal ketone excretion sink; active above BHB 0.5 mmol/L threshold; BHB_RENAL_VMAX = 0.005/min, Km = 2.0
running acidosis accumulator (dimensionless); driven by BHB excess above 3.0 mmol/L; recovers with t1/2 = 45 min when BHB falls below threshold
DKA game-over compartment; triggered when acidosisLoad reaches 600, representing severe metabolic acidosis per Kitabchi 2009 criteria
maximum lipolysis flux constant (mmol/L/min at I = 0)
Hill suppression term for HSL gate: EC50 = 8 mU/L, n = 3; equals 1.0 at I = 0, approaches 0 at high insulin
Hill suppression term for CPT-1 gate: EC50 = 8 mU/L, n = 4; nearly binary — 1.0 at I = 0, approx 0.05 at basal insulin levels
first-order FFA clearance rate constant; t1/2 = ln(2)/k_ffa approx 60 min; represents combined oxidation and re-esterification
net BHB production rate per unit FFA: product of cpt1Activity and BHB_PROD_RATE constant; both gates must be open for nonzero flux
acidosis accumulation rate; excess = BHB - 3.0 when BHB > 3.0; ACCEL term provides progressive acceleration mimicking pH drop kinetics from Kitabchi 2009
insulin-based gate on acidosis accumulation: 0 when insulin suppression <= 0.3, 1 when >= 0.5; prevents nutritional ketosis (insulin-sufficient fasting) from triggering DKA
